was: Weiser State Forest's Greenland Tract, off US 209 near Williamstown: two drive-in motorized roadside sites (G001 on Radar Road, back-in for vehicles up to 34 ft on a steep gravel driveway; G003 on Chestnut Road) plus two hike-in tent sites, in forested uplands. No water, hookups, toilets or trash service (carry in, carry out). Permit and reservation always required; district office 570-875-6450. --Claude

was: The northern no-fee area of the park: a gravel road up the east shore of Horse Run Lake and on into the woods, with sites strung along about 2.5 km. Some sit at the water; the far ones are a long walk from it (a 2022 Campendium reviewer at site 81 puts it at about 1.5 miles). Boat ramp at the south end of the lake. Former AEP ReCreation Land. ODNR gives no length; a 2021 Campendium reviewer with a 26-ft trailer found the sites 'very unlevel'. --Claude

was: USACE campground below Tionesta Dam along Tionesta Creek (Pittsburgh District). Reservation required, on recreation.gov only. 124 back-in full-hookup sites (63 with 50-amp), listed for rigs of about 41-75 ft. A few sites (e.g. 46, 48) back up above the creek; not step-to-water lakefront. --Claude

was: USACE campground on a wooded hillside near East Branch Clarion River Lake (Pittsburgh District). Reservable on recreation.gov only; 21 30-amp electric RV sites, 2 non-electric and 3 tent-only sites plus 4 cabins. Steep terrain; recreation.gov allows RVs of 20-40 ft depending on the site, five pull-throughs; 13'4" powerline clearance on the camp road. Not lakefront. --Claude

was: Allegheny NF ridge-top campground, a base for the Tracy Ridge trail system about 5 miles above the Allegheny Reservoir; concession-run (Allegheny Site Management). Reservable online in summer, with some first-come sites and a first-come fall season; no hookups, vault toilets, hand-pump water in loop E; the dump station is closed (2026). Back-in sites fit RVs ~25-60 ft. Not on the water. --Claude

was: Allegheny NF campground at spring-fed Twin Lake (not the reservoir), eight miles southeast of Kane, with a swimming beach and fishing piers; run with the Friends of Twin Lakes. 50 family sites, 15-amp electric at the lower sites, vault toilets, dump station. Camping by donation (2026); request a site by phone (814-389-3019). A railroad underpass on the FR 191 entrance limits vehicles to under 10 ft tall: use the Dahoga Road entrance from Wilcox, which has no height limit. Near the lake, not lakefront. --Claude

was: Allegheny NF campground beside the Hearts Content old-growth area and Hickory Creek Wilderness, run by concessionaire Allegheny Site Management. 26 single sites with RV spurs (listed 25-45 ft) plus a group site; vault toilets, hand-pump water, dump station, no hookups. Open May 1 to Oct 26, reservable on recreation.gov, and every site also first-come. Not on the water. --Claude

was: NPS concessionaire campground on federal land within Delaware Water Gap National Recreation Area, on Route 209 at Dingmans Ferry. Book direct through the campground's own Campspot link, not Recreation.gov. Riverfront sites on the Delaware are tent-only (no vehicles); the 35 RV sites are in the forest, set back, with 20/30/50-amp electric and water (no sewer; dump stations at the two bathhouses), back-in, rigs to 50 ft; forest boondock sites also take RVs. Dry campground, no generators, no cell service. Usually open late April to early November. Senior/Access passes 50% off up to 2 nights, 10% military. --Claude

was: DCNR state park campground near 88-acre Holman Lake. Reservable via the PA reservation system; 46 sites, 30 of them with water and 50-amp electric (2 of those full hookup, back-in), and a dump station, plus camping cottages and a lodge. Sites sit south of the lake, not lakefront. --Claude

was: DCNR state park campground (Nine Mile Loop) along Nine Mile Run, operated by the Denton Go concession under DCNR. Currently 10 rustic back-in gravel RV sites with electric (DCNR says 11); flush toilets and warm showers in the Adventure Center. Reservable online through Denton Go, not ReserveAmerica. One of PA's highest parks; max RV length not published outside the booking engine. --Claude
